scope: Read-only primary-source research and design critique. No implementation, test, CI, workflow, model, device, engine, or Git mutation.

original_diagnosis.B_original_failure: unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) succeeded; open(/proc/self/setgroups) failed with errno13; conditional-profile join then raised RuntimeError: original kernel denial outside exact syscall/clock interval.
original_diagnosis.exact_rejecting_predicate: MESSAGE audit milliseconds converted to ns are 187040ns below unshare high-resolution realtime start minus the original 2ms lower allowance.
original_diagnosis.journal_receive_clocks: Both original journal reception realtime and monotonic predicates pass. The 301257ns reception lag after failed-open terminal is not the rejecting predicate.
original_diagnosis.nonexecuted_B_checks: No conditional profile admission/load/remove, external full-suite observer, or unittest suite dispatch is evidenced. A successful original suite cannot substitute for B.

primary_sources.claim: Audit serialization divides tv_nsec by 1000000 and emits three fractional digits; this floors the coarse timestamp to milliseconds.
The syscall audit context timestamp is sampled at syscall entry using ktime_get_coarse_real_ts64.
Linux UAPI assigns CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE clock ID5.

The coarse realtime accessor corresponds to CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE and returns the last timer-tick cached value. The documented possible age is not evidence of this runner's actual HZ or a permitted arbitrary tolerance.
__REALTIME_TIMESTAMP and __MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP are microsecond journal reception timestamps, not the audit event timestamp.
_SOURCE_MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP is taken from the kmsg timestamp; replacing the current reception clock with it requires its own provenance and interval contract.

recommended_contract.status: Candidate design requiring planning delta and independent review before code.
recommended_contract.basis: Retain the original audit MESSAGE and all existing high-resolution and journal reception facts. Observe the same Linux CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE basis before original unshare and after the actual failed setgroups open; compare unmodified audit milliseconds against the inclusive millisecond-floored observed coarse bracket.
recommended_contract.versioning: The live consumer must require the new version from its known producer/source/capture contract. Missing both new fields, or stripping both fields and the record's version, must not downgrade an expected-new execution to legacy. Legacy strict2ms joins remain only for explicitly identified historical v1 context, without retroaccepting B.
recommended_contract.sampling_order: Take the pre sample before the original unshare high-resolution start samples. Take the post sample after the existing failed-call terminal samples and first errno have been retained. Link samples to the existing original PID, boot, owner and operation chronology. Preserve the original syscall and exception when sampling fails.
recommended_contract.typing: Require the exact expected version, clock ID5 and clock basis; both sample records must explicitly be available and contain positive integer ns values with booleans excluded. Partial, unavailable, malformed, wrong-clock, or reversed samples cannot authorize profile admission. Equal coarse endpoints are valid.
recommended_contract.join: Floor both genuine sample endpoints to milliseconds and require lower_ms <= original_audit_ms <= upper_ms. Do not rewrite the audit timestamp or add a guessed fine-clock tolerance.
recommended_contract.sampling_failure: Record bounded typed unavailability for clock sampling errors while retaining original call/error facts. Do not turn sampling failure into admission, retry the namespace operation, or swallow cancellation exceptions.
recommended_contract.unchanged_guards: Preserve exact PID/start gate/boot/executable/label/operation/capability joins, original high-resolution chronology, journal reception wall and monotonic interval guards, and existing20s work+10s cleanup, rows/channels/report limits. Do not widen any cap or waive physical provenance.
recommended_contract.clock_getres: Not needed to authorize the observed bracket: resolution does not prove event age or reception delay. It may be bounded informational metadata if independently justified, but must not generate a tolerance or replace genuine endpoint samples.
recommended_contract.alternative: Using journal reception clocks alone loses audit-event provenance. _SOURCE_MONOTONIC_TIMESTAMP is not a drop-in replacement: its kmsg timing and transport differ and need a separately reviewed physical join. An arbitrary 2ms-to10ms widening is unsupported.

requirements_considered.proposal: CI-only per-execution profile requires a physically joined original denial and reviewed exact source.
requirements_considered.design: Preserve bounded namespace diagnosis, exact owner/syscall/errno facts, no global sysctl changes, privileged bypass, blanket skips, runtime bump or automatic retry.
requirements_considered.delta_spec: Preserve CPU selection, six native targets, ABI/scientific settings, one fresh suite child, existing trace/report/channel bounds. Generic errno13 cannot authorize a profile; diagnostic success is not full CI or benchmark acceptance.

limits: The retained A/B executions contain no CLOCK_REALTIME_COARSE endpoint samples; they cannot be retroactively reconstructed or admitted under the candidate contract.
Upstream v6.17 semantics are consistent with the observed original B discrepancy. This is an inference, not a verified source-to-binary proof of the exact Ubuntu azure1022 kernel patch set.
The retained kernel release is exact; installed systemd version, actual HZ and exact Ubuntu kernel source build provenance are not attested here.
Future journal reception guards may independently reject a delayed record; this candidate does not establish that every future CI timing failure will pass.
No implementation, tests, CI rerun, suite acceptance, selected benchmark grant or merge approval is provided.
